This example uses four Visium mouse brain sections from 10x Genomics (two
anterior, two posterior), with each spot labelled by its most enriched of five
marker genes.

<details>
<summary>Setup: download and label the data, define plotting helpers</summary>

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```{r}
#| label: r-setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| results: hide
# Requires Seurat, hdf5r and ggplot2.
library(Seurat)
library(ggplot2)

markers <- c("Mbp", "Slc17a7", "Penk", "Hpca", "Gabra6")
ids <- c(anterior_1 = "V1_Mouse_Brain_Sagittal_Anterior",
         anterior_2 = "V1_Mouse_Brain_Sagittal_Anterior_Section_2",
         posterior_1 = "V1_Mouse_Brain_Sagittal_Posterior",
         posterior_2 = "V1_Mouse_Brain_Sagittal_Posterior_Section_2")
cache <- tools::R_user_dir("friendlycells", "cache")

seurat_objects <- lapply(ids, function(id) {
  dir <- file.path(cache, id)
  if (!dir.exists(file.path(dir, "spatial"))) {
    url <- paste0("https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/spatial-exp/1.1.0/",
                  id, "/", id)
    dir.create(dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
    download.file(paste0(url, "_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5"),
                  file.path(dir, "filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5"))
    download.file(paste0(url, "_spatial.tar.gz"), tar <- tempfile())
    untar(tar, exdir = dir)
  }
  cells <- Load10X_Spatial(dir)
  counts <- as.matrix(GetAssayData(cells, layer = "counts")[markers, ])
  cells$cell_type <- markers[max.col(t(counts / rowMeans(counts)),
                                     ties.method = "first")]
  cells
})

plot_slices <- function(samples) {
  spots <- do.call(rbind, Map(cbind, sample = names(samples), samples))
  ggplot(spots, aes(.data$x, -.data$y, color = .data$label)) +
    geom_point(size = 1.1, stroke = 0) +
    facet_wrap(~sample, nrow = 1) +
    coord_fixed() +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("#CC79A7", "#D55E00", "#0072B2", "#F0E442",
                                  "#009E73")) +
    guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 4))) +
    theme_void(base_size = 14) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_blank())
}

plot_similarity <- function(sim) {
  df <- as.data.frame(as.table(sim))
  lower <- df[as.integer(df$Var1) >= as.integer(df$Var2), ]
  ggplot(lower, aes(.data$Var1, .data$Var2, fill = .data$Freq)) +
    geom_tile() +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", .data$Freq),
                  color = .data$Freq < 0.1),
              size = 5, fontface = "bold", show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("black", "white")) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "inferno", name = "Similarity") +
    coord_fixed() +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    theme(axis.title = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
          text = element_text(face = "bold"))
}
```

## Python

```{python}
#| label: py-setup
#| jupyter_compat: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| results: hide
# Requires squidpy, matplotlib and seaborn.
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import squidpy as sq

markers = ["Mbp", "Slc17a7", "Penk", "Hpca", "Gabra6"]
ids = {
    "anterior_1": "V1_Mouse_Brain_Sagittal_Anterior",
    "anterior_2": "V1_Mouse_Brain_Sagittal_Anterior_Section_2",
    "posterior_1": "V1_Mouse_Brain_Sagittal_Posterior",
    "posterior_2": "V1_Mouse_Brain_Sagittal_Posterior_Section_2",
}
cache = Path.home() / ".cache" / "friendlycells"

adatas = {}
labels = {}
for name, sample_id in ids.items():
    adata = sq.datasets.visium(sample_id, base_dir=cache)
    adata.var_names_make_unique()
    counts = adata[:, markers].X.toarray()
    top = (counts / counts.mean(axis=0)).argmax(axis=1)
    adatas[name] = adata
    labels[name] = np.array(markers)[top]


def plot_slices(samples):
    palette = ["#CC79A7", "#D55E00", "#0072B2", "#F0E442", "#009E73"]
    colors = dict(zip(sorted(markers), palette))
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(samples), layout="constrained")
    for ax, (name, df) in zip(axes, samples.items()):
        ax.scatter(
            df["x"],
            -df["y"],
            c=df["label"].map(colors),
            s=3,
            linewidths=0,
        )
        ax.set_title(name)
        ax.set_aspect("equal")
        ax.axis("off")
    handles = [
        plt.Line2D([], [], marker="o", linestyle="", color=color, label=label)
        for label, color in colors.items()
    ]
    fig.legend(
        handles=handles,
        loc="outside lower center",
        ncol=len(colors),
        frameon=False,
    )
    plt.show()


def plot_similarity(sim):
    style = {"font.size": 14, "font.weight": "bold", "figure.autolayout": True}
    with plt.rc_context(style):
        ax = sns.heatmap(
            sim,
            mask=np.tril(np.ones(sim.shape, dtype=bool), k=-1),
            annot=True,
            fmt=".2f",
            cmap="inferno",
            vmin=0,
            vmax=1,
            square=True,
            cbar_kws={"label": "Similarity"},
        )
        ax.invert_yaxis()
        plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha="right")
    plt.show()
```
:::

</details>

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

Each sample is a data frame of spot positions (in full-resolution image
pixels) and labels:

```{r}
#| label: r-samples
library(friendlycells)

samples <- lapply(seurat_objects, function(cells) {
  coords <- GetTissueCoordinates(cells)
  data.frame(x = coords$x, y = coords$y, label = cells$cell_type[coords$cell],
             row.names = coords$cell)
})
head(samples$anterior_1)
```

```{r}
#| label: r-slices
#| fig-dpi: 300
#| fig-retina: 1
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.5
plot_slices(samples)
```

```{r}
#| label: r-similarity
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 5
#| out-width: 60%
sim <- spatial_similarity(samples, "x", "y", "label")
round(sim, 2)
plot_similarity(sim)
```

## Python

Each sample is a DataFrame of spot positions (in full-resolution image
pixels) and labels:

```{python}
#| label: py-samples
#| jupyter_compat: true
from friendlycells import spatial_similarity

samples = {
    name: pd.DataFrame({
        "x": adata.obsm["spatial"][:, 0],
        "y": adata.obsm["spatial"][:, 1],
        "label": labels[name],
    }, index=adata.obs_names)
    for name, adata in adatas.items()
}
print(samples["anterior_1"].head())
```

```{python}
#| label: py-slices
#| fig-dpi: 300
#| fig-retina: 1
#| jupyter_compat: true
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.5
plot_slices(samples)
```

```{python}
#| label: py-similarity
#| jupyter_compat: true
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 5
#| out-width: 60%
sim = spatial_similarity(samples, "x", "y", "label")
print(sim.round(2))
plot_similarity(sim)
```
:::

The anterior sections are most similar to each other, as are the posterior
sections, while anterior and posterior sections are dissimilar.
